newsitem.title: GERMANY: Millions of children die from hunger each year - UN. [CORRECTED 16:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Millions of children die from hunger each year - UN. [CORRECTED 16:45 GMT]

text.p: The U.N. children's fund (UNICEF) said on Monday millions of children were still dying from hunger and disease, despite the organisation's vow to fight the problem at a 1990 summit.

UNICEF director Carol Bellamy said in the latest report on child mortalilty presented to journalists in Cologne the food situation in developing countries had barely improved in the last six years and most deaths were due to undernourishment.
(Corrects to make clear that Bellamy was not at the presentation).
She said that although one million fewer children died this year than in 1990, the annual figure of over 12 million child deaths was alarmingly high.

Citing a report produced by its German office, UNICEF said it was also concerned about an increase in the number of women who died because of childbirth. This figure edged up to 585,000 from about 500,000 six years ago.
At the 1990 world summit on children, UNICEF pledged to fight child deaths in developing countries caused by disease and hunger in an attempt to improve the situation by the year 2000.
Bellamy said 80 percent of children were now innoculated against the most serious diseases and that doctors should have eradicated some of them entirely by the year 2000.

Some progress had been made fighting other often fatal diseases with a sugar and salt solution. But UNICEF said children in many countries suffered from a lack of vitamin A and that hygiene had deteriorated in many cities.
